content.user_title: Scale Python Data Workloads with Dask
content.value_statement: Large datasets can exceed memory or make pandas and NumPy workflows too slow. This skill guides Dask collections, schedulers, chunking, and distributed execution.
actual_capabilities: Selects Dask DataFrame, Array, Bag, Futures, or scheduler patterns for the requested workload.
Explains lazy task graphs, compute, persist, partitioning, and chunk sizing.
Provides patterns for CSV, Parquet, JSON, Zarr, HDF5, and NetCDF workloads.
Guides local thread, process, synchronous, and distributed scheduler choices.
Suggests dashboard-based diagnosis for memory, task graph, and parallelism problems.
Outlines ETL, array, and custom future workflows.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples but does not execute or benchmark Dask workloads.
Cannot determine optimal sizing without dataset, memory, workload, and cluster details.
Does not replace Dask documentation for version-specific APIs or deployment settings.
Assumes Python and relevant Dask packages are already installed.

use_cases.title: Scale a tabular ETL pipeline
use_cases.description: Convert multi-file pandas processing into a partitioned Dask DataFrame workflow with efficient loading, aggregation, and Parquet output.

use_cases.title: Process scientific arrays
use_cases.description: Choose array chunks and storage formats for larger-than-memory calculations using NumPy-style operations.

use_cases.title: Plan distributed task execution
use_cases.description: Select schedulers and Futures patterns for custom jobs that require dependencies, monitoring, and controlled data movement.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Dask collection
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to process {data_type} totaling {size} on {resources}. Recommend the right Dask collection and explain the choice.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a pandas workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this pandas workflow into a Dask DataFrame approach: {workflow}. Explain partitioning, lazy evaluation, and when results enter memory.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Dask workload and symptoms: {details}. Identify likely task graph, partition, scheduler, or memory issues and propose measurable checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design distributed execution
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Dask architecture for {workload} across {cluster}. Cover scheduler choice, worker layout, data movement, persistence, monitoring, and failure handling.

output_examples.input: Choose a Dask approach for 400 GB of daily Parquet files with groupby aggregations.
output: Use Dask DataFrame because the workload is partitioned, tabular, and based on familiar pandas operations.
Read Parquet directly, filter columns early, and align partitions with available worker memory.
Inspect the dashboard before persisting reused intermediate results.

output_examples.input: Explain why a Dask Array calculation creates millions of small tasks.
output: The chunks are probably too small or repeated operations expanded the task graph.
Increase chunk sizes, combine block operations, and inspect graph size before computation.
Validate changes on representative data and compare task count, memory, and runtime.

output_examples.input: Recommend a scheduler for CPU-heavy Python text parsing on one machine.
output_examples.output: Use the process scheduler because pure Python parsing is usually limited by the interpreter lock. Compare it with threads using a representative sample.

best_practices: Provide dataset size, file format, machine memory, core count, and cluster details.
Test on representative samples before scaling to the full dataset.
Use the Dask dashboard to validate task, memory, and worker assumptions.
anti_patterns: Do not load the full dataset with pandas before converting it to Dask.
Do not call compute repeatedly when independent results can be computed together.
Do not create millions of tiny partitions or tasks without measuring scheduler overhead.

faq.question: When should I use Dask DataFrame?
faq.answer: Use it for partitioned tabular data when pandas-style operations fit the workload and the data is large or parallel processing helps.

faq.question: When should I use Dask Array?
faq.answer: Use it for chunked numerical data and NumPy-style operations, especially with Zarr, HDF5, NetCDF, or larger-than-memory arrays.

faq.question: Does this skill run a Dask cluster?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation and configuration guidance but does not deploy, start, or administer clusters.

faq.question: How do I choose chunk or partition sizes?
faq.answer: Start from worker memory, core count, operation type, and storage layout. Then measure memory, task count, and runtime with representative data.

faq.question: Can Dask accelerate every pandas or NumPy workload?
faq.answer: No. Small datasets, unsupported operations, poor partitioning, or high scheduling overhead can make simpler local tools faster.

faq.question: Which scheduler should I choose?
faq.answer: Use threads for numeric work, processes for Python-heavy work, synchronous mode for debugging, and distributed scheduling for monitoring or clusters.
